focus: CustomChannelMessageValidator — subject validation parity with body
summary: All 20 tests PASS. CustomChannelMessageValidator correctly validates :subject using the same regex and error message as :body. The validator is registered on both attributes without conditional guards, handles nil and empty string gracefully, and catches all {{Placeholder}} patterns including spaced, dotted, uppercase, lowercase, and mixed-case variants. Single braces, empty braces, and normal text correctly pass validation.

results.details: Error correctly added: 'Message not sent. An invalid placeholder formatted like {{Something}} was found.'
No :subject errors for clean text
Nil value handled gracefully — regex =~ nil returns nil, no error added
Empty string does not match {{...}} regex

results.test: 5A. Both body and subject with {{Var}} get errors
results.details: Validator adds errors to both attributes independently

results.test: 5B. Only body with {{Var}} → only body gets error
results.details: Clean subject not affected by body validation

results.test: 5C. Only subject with {{Var}} → only subject gets error
results.details: Clean body not affected by subject validation
Both clean values pass

results.test: 5E. Same error message on both attributes
results.details: Both produce: 'Message not sent. An invalid placeholder formatted like {{Something}} was found.'
Exactly 1 CustomChannelMessageValidator on each attribute in ChannelMessage.validators_on

results.test: 5G. Subject validator has no conditional guards (always runs)
results.details: No :if or :unless options — validates on every ChannelMessage
Regex \s* handles inner whitespace
Regex [\w.]+ matches dotted identifiers
Case-insensitive flag handles uppercase
Lowercase identifiers caught
\w includes digits
Single braces correctly not flagged (requires double braces)
Plain text passes
Empty inner content (whitespace only) not matched by [\w.]+
Empty double braces not matched — regex requires at least one \w or . character

findings.description: CustomChannelMessageValidator uses deprecated `record.errors[attribute] << msg` syntax (line 13). Rails 6.1 emits a deprecation warning recommending `record.errors.add(attribute, msg)` instead. This is a pre-existing issue not introduced by the email-subjects feature, but it will fire on every subject validation now that subject is validated. Not blocking.
